thread:
maya: kicking off a 1-hour sim soak in staging to validate per-org and per-key rate limits + burst behavior. starting 10:30 PT. load profile: 10k rps ramp -> 25k, 5% of keys flagged as bursty.

dan: ok. which runner/region? loadbot in us-west1? will we exercise canary routing + fallback?

maya: yes loadbot -> staging cluster A (canary routing enabled). plan: two traffic types: keyed (X-API-Key) and org-wide (no key). keyed includes keys across free/prod/dedicated tiers.

liam: add telemetry flags: include x-debug-ratelimit in responses and attach a spike trace id so console can correlate. need metrics for token_bucket_fill, last_regen_ts, and 429_reason.

sara: dashboards ready: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/staging/rl/simsoak - I've added a 429 lane and per-key p50/p95/p99 panels. will add an alert if 429 rate > 1% for 5m.

maya: note: we'll run canary with a 'soft-fail' policy so overloaded workers return 429+Retry-After and a hint body suggesting dedicated capacity when applicable.

dan: quick internal debate: should SDKs auto-retry 429s? last incident showed it can mask capacity problems. i vote fail-fast.

liam: agree fail-fast by default. but for test coverage we should include an "sdk-retry" toggle in loadbot so we can simulate both behaviors.

sara: also ensure quota headers match spec: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (seconds). some partners expect that exact shape.

loadbot: starting run now. command: ./loadbot --profile keyed-burst --rps 10000 --ramp 30m --spike 5% --headers 'X-API-Key: KEY_*' --sdk-retry=false

maya: initial observations after 10m: per-key 99p latency stable, a small number of keys get 429s when simulated burst exceeds bucket_size. telemetry shows regen lag ~1200ms for affected keys.

dan: can you paste short logs for one key?

maya: paste:
```
[10:42:11] key=KEY_42 status=429 bucket_tokens=0 regen_ms=1203 route=canary-1
[10:42:12] key=KEY_42 status=200 bucket_tokens=10 regen_ms=0 route=canary-1
```

liam: that matches token-bucket behavior. curious if org-level aggregate is throttling those keys sooner — could be org-burst window too small.

sara: on the dashboard I see per-org throttles tripping slightly before per-key. @maya can you bump org-burst multiplier to 2x and re-run a 5m segment?

maya: toggled org-burst to 2x. re-running the 5m segment now.

loadbot: re-run complete for window 10:55-11:00. result summary: 429s reduced by ~40%, p95 latency unchanged.

dan: good. next concrete actions: (1) add e2e test asserting X-RateLimit-* headers present and correct, (2) document SDK retry default as "off" and add guidance in clients, (3) update rollout UX to surface throttled keys in console with recommended actions (upgrade, shard keys, contact success).

sara: I'll open a quick PR to annotate the dashboard and wire the alert. also adding an alert runbook referencing the Retry-After header behavior.

liam: also add telemetry flag 'fallback_invoked' when routing falls back to cheaper model or lower-tier pool due to capacity. helps correlate QoE drops.

maya: capturing everything in the run report and creating tickets for SDK docs + e2e test. thanks all :raised_hands: 

console-bot: run-report uploaded: https://artifacts/internal/runs/1809001111/keyed-throttle-sim-soak/report.json
